_tier_comment: READ THE NAV, NOT THE TEMPLATE. ampersand-nav/src/amp-nav.js records ticktickclock as { place: 3, rung: 'spec' } at line 688, and its own renderPlacement() emits the layer sentence for place 2 ONLY — place 3 gets 'a specification in the ComputeDriven world' plus a link to the spec, and place 4 gets attribution only. Three variants, not two. Writing a layer sentence here would put the band in direct contradiction with the nav rendered immediately beneath it. Checked 2026-08-17 by reading amp-nav.js; the nav source is lane N's and was NOT edited.

question: Can a monitor learn from every tick and still remember last season?
_spec_url_comment: RULED BY TRAVIS 2026-08-17: 'all the docs have that # in them'. This record held the bare, hash-less form until then, and the five links it fed on the page went with it. BE ACCURATE ABOUT WHAT CHANGED: the bare form is NOT a dead link — measured 2026-08-17 it returns HTTP 200, text/html, a real prerendered page. The #/ form returns the 10.5 MB docsify shell that renders the document client-side. Both resolve; Travis is ruling the canonical form, not repairing a 404. The lane that wrote the bare form chose it deliberately because it resolves without JavaScript, which is true and is now overruled. launch-gate.mjs refuses any docs.ampersandboxdesign.com link that is not on the #/ route, so the two forms cannot drift apart again.
_rung_witness_comment: SHELL.md r5. A blanket 'any pending gate blocks the rung' rule cannot work here: independent_implementation is pending forever by construction. This names the ONE gate that witnesses the rung — the document exists, is internally consistent, and every section number this page cites resolves in it — and launch-gate.mjs refuses if that named gate is not approved with its evidence.
surface_rung_covers: one document — the v0.1 draft at docs/spec/README.md — and the three capability contracts it declares. No implementation exists anywhere: no mix project, no MCP server, no stream
_nav_property_comment: RULED BY TRAVIS 2026-08-17: 'the ampersand-nav needs to be on each website!'. This surface, and four siblings, dropped <amp-nav> when they adopted the shell — each lane independently, to keep the page's content shipping with zero JavaScript, and no ruling had ever been made. It has now been made. This is the key the shared nav files this property under in ampersand-nav/src/amp-nav.js; build-site.mjs refuses to emit if the vendored amp-nav.js does not know it, because an unknown key renders an empty bar rather than an error. NOTE, and it is expected: the vendored copy in this repo is the DEPLOYED 51,428-byte revision, which has no renderPlacement(), so the nav renders without a placement band until lane N syncs the 65,544-byte source. That is lane N's to fix and a vendored copy must not be hand-edited to add it.
_nav_stack_comment: SHELL.md r6: the stacking breakpoint belongs to the surface, not the shell. r5 gave 430px, measured on a four-item nav; the bendrune lane measured 780px on six. Measured on this nav and recorded here; launch-gate.mjs checks the stylesheet against this number.
_nav_labels_comment: SHELL.md r11: a stacking breakpoint measured against labels that can be renamed without notice is a stale number waiting to happen — renaming one item to 'Correct us' once moved a wrap point 538 → 576, past a 560 breakpoint, marooning the logo in a broken two-row state. So the labels the measurement was taken with are recorded here and launch-gate.mjs refuses when the emitted nav drifts from them. BISECTED, not computed (r11), in agent-browser session 'navback' on 2026-08-17: 2+ rows at <= 635px, one clean row at >= 636px. Re-bisected AFTER <amp-nav> was restored and the number did not move — the portfolio nav is position:fixed chrome above the page and takes no width from .top.

status.statement: A draft specification and three machine-readable capability contracts. The contracts were re-read from disk during this build and every operation they declare was matched against the operation tables in the spec; the spec's own structure, including its performance table, was recounted from the file.
status.source: build-site.mjs on 2026-08-17: it parses docs/spec/README.md with fenced code blocks stripped, counts its numbered headings, its task boxes, its acceptance criteria and its performance rows, and compares the operation tables in §6 against records/contracts/*.contract.json — which are byte-identical copies of the files in AmpersandBoxDesign/contracts/v0.1.0/, checked by SHA-256 on every build run in the portfolio tree.
status.limit: This establishes that a document exists and that it does not contradict the contract files beside it. It does not establish that any of it works. The nine figures in §10 are targets, not measurements — nothing has been compiled, so no tick has ever been processed, no anomaly detected and no forecast made. The catastrophic-forgetting claim, the sub-millisecond detection latency and the hundred thousand concurrent streams are design intentions written down. The spec's own Pre-Phase exists precisely because those assumptions are unvalidated, and it has not been started.

advance.requires: A mix project in this repository whose test suite runs. The nearest honest step is the spec's own FV-2 — four GenServers ticking at different intervals with events promoting from the fast tier to the slow one — because it needs no model, no ONNX and no dataset, and it is the assumption the whole multi-timescale argument rests on. One feasibility validation with a result would move this rung; a hundred more pages of specification would not.

artifacts.name: The v0.1 draft specification
artifacts.detail: Fourteen numbered sections covering an adaptive state-space anomaly engine, a multi-timescale forecast engine, a pattern engine over Matrix Profile, epoch-aware delta-CRDT replication, an Ecto data model, a 30-week roadmap and five architecture decision records. It is a design document with Elixir type declarations in it, not Elixir.
artifacts.witness: The file, re-read and recounted by this build. Every § number cited on this page was resolved against its real headings, with fenced code blocks stripped first.

artifacts.name: Three &time capability contracts
artifacts.detail: &time.anomaly, &time.forecast and &time.pattern as JSON: named operations with typed input and output slots, whether each is deterministic and whether it has side effects, and the primitives they accept from and feed into. A declaration a client could be written against — not a service a client can call.
artifacts.witness: Byte-identical copies of AmpersandBoxDesign/contracts/v0.1.0/, compared by SHA-256 during this build. Every operation they name was matched against the tables in §6 of the spec.

artifacts.name: The PULSE loop manifest
artifacts.detail: A five-phase loop — retrieve_window, route_inference, act_publish, learn_outcome, consolidate_epoch — declared in prose, with its closure, cadence, substrates and cross-loop signals. This is the surface that corresponds most directly to PULSE, the temporal algebra: every phase maps to one of PULSE's five canonical kinds.
artifacts.witness: Extracted from the spec by this build. It is prose in a Markdown table: no ticktickclock.temporal_intelligence.pulse.json exists in PULSE/manifests/, so nothing can validate it against the PULSE v0.1 schema.

unmeasured.name: FV-1 — a state-space model that runs without EXLA
unmeasured.detail: Load a Mamba-style selective state-space model through Bumblebee and ONNX, run a synthetic stream through it, and measure per-tick latency and resident memory. The spec carries its own fallback — an exponential moving average with a Z-score — which is an admission that the headline architecture might not be reachable here at all.
unmeasured.needs: A model that exists in ONNX form, and a machine to time it on.

unmeasured.name: FV-2 — multi-timescale consolidation as ticking GenServers
unmeasured.detail: Four supervised processes ticking at four intervals, with events promoting from the fast tier to the medium and slow ones, under sustained load. No forgetting is the claim the whole product is named for, and this is the smallest experiment that could contradict it.
unmeasured.needs: A mix project and a few hundred lines of Elixir. No model, no dataset, no GPU.

unmeasured.name: FV-3 — delta-CRDT convergence for temporal state
unmeasured.detail: Five nodes, a partition during active detection, and a check that the anomaly history converges with no phantom detections and none lost. The same experiment GeoFleetic needs for spatial twins, which is either an efficiency or a shared single point of failure.
unmeasured.needs: A cluster of five BEAM nodes, which is a laptop.

unmeasured.name: §10 — nine performance targets, none measured
unmeasured.detail: Sub-millisecond detection per tick, fifty-millisecond forecasts, a hundred thousand concurrent streams on one node, zero temporal forgetting by design. Every one is a target in a table in an unimplemented specification. This page used to print three of them as if they were readings from something running.
unmeasured.needs: Something to measure. That is the whole of it.

unmeasured.name: Any implementation at all
unmeasured.detail: No mix project, no supervision tree, no MCP server, no TimescaleDB migration. The eight MCP tools named in §8 do not exist as code anywhere; the eight names are the whole of them.
unmeasured.needs: Phase 0 of the roadmap, which is scheduled after a Pre-Phase that has not begun.

zero_counts.label: Lines of TickTickClock implementation code
zero_counts.witness: There is no mix.exs, no lib/, no .ex and no .exs in this repository outside old_scraps/, and no TickTickClock code in any other repository in the portfolio. Recounted by this build.

zero_counts.label: Ticks ever ingested
zero_counts.witness: No stream process has ever been started, because no code exists to start one. The counter that used to stand on this page and read zero was not measuring anything; it was a zero drawn next to a label.

zero_counts.label: Performance targets measured
zero_counts.witness: §10 declares nine of them. This build counts the rows in that table and the number of them with a witness, and the second number is zero.

contract_agreement.label: The operation tables in §6 and the contract JSON declare the same operations
contract_agreement.description: Each of &time.anomaly, &time.forecast and &time.pattern is declared twice — once as a Markdown table in the spec, once as a JSON contract file in AmpersandBoxDesign. Two hand-maintained copies of one list drift. This build compares them and refuses on any difference in either direction.
contract_agreement.evidence: detect/enrich/learn, predict/explain/enrich/learn, detect/summarize/enrich — 10 operations, no additions and no omissions on either side.

feasibility_validation.label: Pre-Phase FV-1 … FV-4 have been run and have results
feasibility_validation.description: The spec makes the case itself: these are the highest-risk assumptions and they are to be validated before the implementation is committed to. None has been started.

performance_targets.label: Any figure in §10 has been measured on something running
performance_targets.description: Nine targets, zero measurements. Three of them were published on this page as statistics until this revision.

implementation.label: A mix project exists whose test suite runs
implementation.description: The condition for the in_tree rung. Phase 0 of the roadmap.

independent_implementation.label: Someone who is not us implements &time.anomaly against this contract
independent_implementation.description: The condition for the external rung. Pending by construction, and it does not block the rung this surface claims — SHELL.md r5, rung_witness.

pulse_manifest_file.label: The PULSE loop manifest exists as a file that validates against the schema
pulse_manifest_file.description: §7.1 declares a PULSE-conforming loop in prose. PULSE/manifests/ holds manifests for graphonomous, prism, agentromatic and the two embodiment loops — not this one, which is awkward for the surface that corresponds most directly to the temporal algebra. Until the manifest is a file, PULSE/schemas/pulse-loop-manifest.v0.1.json cannot be run against it.
